name: starting architecture
last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so the analysis rests on how well each design fits the task. In this world a brick's fate depends on where it lands. The per-layer footprint head (r2c1) makes the "does it land at z and match the target" check local to one layer, so it is the strongest guess. All three trials ran without errors, and the 1-epoch run reached 315k steps within the time limit. This is the last round and selection takes the best trial, so I combine plausible gains instead of testing one change at a time. (1) 1 epoch plus whole-episode, longer-horizon rollouts: the most fresh designs, with credit for irreversible mistakes. (2) A shared 3x3 conv within each layer before the footprint pooling, so the head can see same-layer neighbours when choosing how to split a layer into bricks. (3) Column attention with 1 epoch, which recovers the samples lost to the attention block's extra compute.
